title: Replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 311/30)
description: The firm is on day 311/30 of a fixed trading window. Fixed-window evaluation creates end-of-horizon distortions: agents and managers behave differently when the 'clock is running out'. More importantly, when day 30 ends, institutional memory resets. Proposal: remove the 30-day limit. Run perpetually. Generate a quarterly benchmark report (vs. SPY, QQQ, sector ETFs) every 63 trading days. Evaluate the firm on rolling 30/63/252-day Sharpe ratio, not a single fixed window. This is how real hedge funds measure themselves.
auto_fix_hint: In state.json, replace `paper_day` counter with `trading_day_total` (never resets). Add `quarterly_benchmark_day` that triggers a benchmark report every 63 days. In main.py, remove the day-30 termination condition. Report generator shows trailing 30/63-day Sharpe vs. benchmark instead of 'Day X/30'.
signature: replace 30-day fixed evaluation window with a rolling perpetual model (currently day 311/30)

title: Replace fixed R&D cadence with event-triggered research cycles
description: R&D last ran 228h ago and fires on a fixed 3-day clock. Markets don't care about our schedule. High-conviction opportunities emerge after earnings beats, sector breakouts, and macro prints — not on a Tuesday-every-three-days basis. Proposal: keep the 3-day heartbeat, but add event triggers: any sector ETF moving >3% in a day forces an immediate targeted R&D cycle for that sector only. Canary YELLOW triggers a full cycle. This would have caught the DIS move that fired ORANGE today.
auto_fix_hint: In canary_agent.py: when a sector ETF moves >3% intraday, write `data/rd_trigger.json` with the sector name. In main.py Step 3c: if rd_trigger.json exists and is <4h old, run rd_team_leader.py --sector <name> regardless of 3-day cadence. Delete the trigger file after the cycle completes.
signature: replace fixed r&d cadence with event-triggered research cycles

title: Pre-trade devil's advocate: adversarial challenge before high-conviction buys
description: The BUY pipeline has no adversarial check. Review Agent recommends → Manager Agent approves → trade executes. The IRM reviews decisions post-hoc but can't stop a trade in-flight. Proposal: for any BUY with conviction ≥4★, spawn a 'BearCaseAgent' that reads the same thesis and produces a structured counter-argument: what would have to be true for this trade to fail? What's the base rate of success for this sector/pattern? Does the canary context invalidate the thesis? Manager Agent sees both the bull and bear case before deciding. This won't block good trades — it will surface hidden risks on marginal ones.
auto_fix_hint: Add BearCaseAgent class to manager_agent.py. Instantiate it inline when conviction >= 4 before placing the order. It reads the pick's sector, RSI, recent news context (from canary/geopolitical data), and writes a structured counter-case to `data/bear_cases.json`. Manager Agent's final decision logs both cases for IRM post-trade review.
signature: pre-trade devil's advocate: adversarial challenge before high-conviction buys

title: No sector concentration heat map in daily reports
description: The daily HTML report shows positions but not sector concentration. The CRO tracks concentration risk internally but it never appears visually in the Chairman's daily email.

title: Risk/reward ratio not tracked per position
description: The firm tracks win/loss streak and P&L percentage, but not the risk/reward ratio at entry (potential upside vs downside based on stop-loss and take-profit levels). Over time, a low average R/R ratio erodes profitability even with a high win rate.
auto_fix_hint: At BUY execution, calculate and store `stop_price = entry_price × (1 - STOP_LOSS_PCT)` and `target_price = entry_price × (1 + TAKE_PROFIT_PCT)` in buy_log. Report average R/R in the trade review.
signature: risk/reward ratio not tracked per position

title: SMTP email sends are synchronous and block the pipeline
description: Every email in the pipeline (daily report, CoS brief, IRM review, board minutes) blocks the main thread until SMTP completes. Gmail SMTP timeout is 30 seconds. If Gmail is slow or the network is flaky, the entire pipeline stalls at every email step.
auto_fix_hint: Wrap email sends in a background thread (threading.Thread) or use asyncio. Store emails in a queue and flush at pipeline end. This would also allow retry on transient SMTP failures.
signature: smtp email sends are synchronous and block the pipeline
